In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have provided a framework for building agents on top of existing data structures, and have shown how to implement such agents in polynomial time.
we have identified a large class of agents (called regular agents) that are both computationally and epistemically attractive.
we have provided a complete and efficient implementation of regular agents, and that the reasonable status set is a polynomially computable semantics for these agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a framework for building heterogeneous agent systems, and have identified a class of agents for which the reasonable status set agent semantics can be computed efficiently.

we have provided an implementation architecture for agent systems, and we have identified a class of agent programs (regular agents) for which this architecture provides an implementation that is both computationally and epistemically optimal.
we have provided the first complete semantics for agent programs, and have provided a polynomial implementation for a large fragment of this semantics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the class of regular agents, we can compute a semantics that is epistemically most desired, and that is also polynomially computable.
